+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, here we have three different kinds of effects that, in my opinion, could easily be used by researchers and D-class to help prevent triggering other SCP objects with visual, vocal, or auditory triggers. Got an SCP you need to experiment with that has a visual trigger, like SCP-1753? Have the D-class use an instance of SCP-894-3. Need to work around an object with an auditory effect, like SCP-2599? Fire up the ol' SCP-894-2. Need to move an object that has a vocalization trigger, like SCP-1752? Use of SCP-894-1 can help you out. As such, I am proposing the following addition at the article's end.

Adding this:

Use of instances of SCP-894 by research staff and D-class personnel to prevent the effects of objects possessing visual, vocal, or auditory triggers, such as SCP-1753, SCP-1752, and SCP-2599 respectively, has proven effective means of facilitating ongoing containment.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's got potential, but you need to elaborate a whole lot more. Under what circumstances were it's properties brought to the attention of the Foundation? Could it be used to nullify the powers of SCP-239? If it induces physical silence, could it also silence their thoughts to telepathic SCPs?
Also, it is a bit… tame by general SCP standards - try, say, having victims silenced for much longer - perhaps permanently - or their tongues burnt out unless certain precautions are taken.
The main problem, though, is definitely length. Pad it out a bit, maybe see if you can find a good image.
